Creative design thinking is a specific type of creativity that requires a mix of general and specific knowledge, abilities, and personal characteristics.

(1) creative design thinking is a complex and multifaceted process, which includes a range of skills, abilities, and dispositions; (2) creative design thinking involves a range of specific and general abilities; (3) creative design thinking requires both general and task-specific abilities; (4) domain-general abilities are important for creative design thinking; and (5) domain-specific abilities are important for creativity in design thinking.
creative design thinking is a domain-general skill that is not dependent upon domain-specific knowledge or experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how creative thinking in design thinking relates to creativity in general, and how this knowledge can inform teaching and learning in design thinking.
how the general skills and characteristics of creativity are applied in the specific context of design thinking.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field is not yet ready to make such a statement about the degree of domain specificity or generalization in creative design thinking.
creative design thinking is a domain-general process that can be applied to many different domains.

creative design thinking requires a mix, or balance, of domain-specific and domain general abilities, skills, and personal attributes, with the balance depending on the specific design thinking context and task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
creative design thinking is a domain-specific task, yet there are many aspects that are domain-general and can be taught and learned.
creative design thinking is a domain-general skill with domain-specific elements.
the domain-general and domain-specific aspects of creativity are not necessarily mutually exclusive, and that both are relevant to the development of creative design thinking.
The main takeaway from our work is that

creative design thinking has some similarities to other forms of creative thinking, but that it has unique characteristics that require a more specific focus on certain domain-general skills and personal characteristics than has previously been suggested.
design thinking is not a single, unified skill but is instead a complex set of skills, and the extent to which those skills are domain-specific and/or domain-general is not yet clear.
creative design thinking can be considered a domain-general skill that can be applied across contexts.
